c.tagline: Bai heartland between Cangshan's peaks and Erhai's shore — old-town lanes, lake villages and mountain air.

taxi.fareNote: Meters are used in the city, but Didi (China's Uber) is far easier for foreigners and priced in-app. Payment almost everywhere is by Alipay or WeChat Pay — link a card in advance, as cash and foreign cards are rarely accepted.

emergency.note: 110 reaches police and 120 is the ambulance line; English is limited, so having your hotel or a translation app on hand helps.

avoid.reason: Watch for overpriced 'tea ceremony' invitations, pushy tour touts and inflated boat/photo fees around the Old Town and Erhai Lake.

hood_desc: The walled Bai-heritage old town (Dali Ancient City) with its stone gates, marble-paved lanes, tie-dye workshops, temples and countless guesthouses; the classic first-timer base, wonderfully walkable and lively day and night.

The bar-and-cafe spine of the old town running down to the West Gate, packed with live-music bars, street food, craft stalls and backpacker hangouts; the heart of Dali's nightlife and people-watching.

The western lakeshore villages such as Caicun just outside the old town, where waterfront guesthouses and cafes look across Erhai to the mountains; a mellow middle ground between old-town buzz and lake calm.

A restored Bai fishing town on Erhai's northeast shore, famed for sunrise lake views, whitewashed courtyard inns and romantic waterfront cafes; quieter, scenic and popular with couples, about an hour from the old town.

A historic Bai market town north of the old town with grand courtyard mansions, a lively morning market and the surrounding rapeseed fields; authentic, unhurried and loved by culture-minded travelers.

water.note: Drink bottled or boiled water, as locals do; tap water is not potable.

transit.hours: City and village buses run roughly 6:30 AM to 9:00 PM; there is no metro, so Didi and taxis cover late evenings.
transit.note: Dali has no metro; getting around is by city bus, buses linking the old town with Xiaguan (Dali city) and lakeshore villages, plus taxis and the Didi app. The old town itself is walkable, and cycling the Erhai loop is popular.
transit.pay: Buses take exact-change cash or a scan of Alipay/WeChat Pay; taxis and Didi are paid the same way. Mobile payment is near-universal.

food.name: Bai Sour and Spicy Fish
food.desc: Erhai lake fish simmered with pickled chilies, green peppercorn and sour plum or passion fruit - the signature Bai clay-pot dish of the lakeshore.

places.name: Caicun Fishing Village Eateries
places.note: Closest lake-fish houses to the Old Town; fish picked from the tank and cooked to order.

places.name: Shuanglang Village Lakeside Restaurants
places.note: Bai family kitchens with terrace tables over the water, best known for the sour-spicy fish pot.

places.name: Renmin Road Restaurant Strip
places.note: Rows of Bai home-style kitchens serving the fish casserole in portions sized for two.

food.name: Rushan (Grilled Milk Fan)
food.desc: Fan-shaped sheets of Bai cow-milk cheese, grilled over charcoal until blistered and brushed with rose jam or sprinkled with sugar and chili.

places.name: Fuxing Road Snack Stalls
places.note: The main Old Town snack run; charcoal grills turn out rushan sheets all afternoon and evening.

places.name: Xizhou Sifang Street Market
places.note: Xizhou is the Bai dairy heartland - rushan here is made in the village that invented it.

places.name: Zhoucheng Village Market
places.note: Tie-dye village market with Bai grandmothers grilling rushan beside the stalls.

food.name: Erkuai (Pressed Rice Cake)
food.desc: Dali's staple rice cake, either grilled flat and wrapped around youtiao with sesame and chili sauce, or sliced into ribbons and stir-fried with ham and eggs.

places.name: Dali Old Town Morning Market
places.note: Breakfast griddles fold shao erkuai to order; the cheapest and freshest version in town.

places.name: Xiaguan Breakfast Shops
places.note: Locals rate Xiaguan for stir-fried and soup erkuai; far fewer tourists than the Old Town.

places.name: Fuxing Road Snack Stalls
places.note: Convenient run of griddle stalls for grilled erkuai wraps between sights.

food.name: Xizhou Baba
food.desc: Layered wheat flatbread baked in a charcoal-topped pan until flaky - savory with pork and spring onion, or sweet with rose sugar.

places.name: Xizhou Sifang Street Bakers
places.note: The dish's home village; ovens on the square bake sweet and savory baba all day.

places.name: Xizhou Morning Market
places.note: Village market stalls sell baba straight from the pan alongside Bai produce.

places.name: Dali Old Town South Gate Stalls
places.note: Handy carts by the gate if you are not making the trip out to Xizhou.

food.name: Tile-Roasted Pork (Wa Kao Rou)
food.desc: Thin pork belly grilled on a curved roof tile over coals, wrapped in lettuce or mint with pickled vegetables and a dry chili dip.

places.name: Yeyu Road Grill Houses
places.note: Quieter lane of local grill restaurants doing tile-roasted pork and skewers after dark.

places.name: Renmin Road Restaurant Strip
places.note: Several Bai kitchens keep tile grills going at the table; good for groups.

places.name: Xizhou Sifang Street Market
places.note: Village grills serve tile-roasted pork with local pickles and herbs.

food.name: Yunnan Wild Mushroom Hotpot
food.desc: Chicken broth loaded with matsutake, boletus and other Yunnan fungi, timed by the server - summer and autumn are peak mushroom season.

places.name: Renmin Road Restaurant Strip
places.note: Mushroom hotpot specialists cluster here in wild-fungus season, July to October.

places.name: Dali Old Town Morning Market
places.note: See the day's fungi haul before you order; several cooked stalls sit alongside.

places.name: Shuanglang Village Lakeside Restaurants
places.note: Lake-view hotpot houses combining wild mushrooms with local free-range chicken.

food.name: Bai Three-Course Tea (Santaocha)
food.desc: Bai ceremonial tea in three cups - bitter, then sweet with walnut and rushan, then a peppery aftertaste cup - often served with music and dance.

places.name: Yan Family Compound
places.note: Grand Bai merchant courtyard where the three-course tea ceremony is performed with live music.

places.name: Zhoucheng Village Courtyards
places.note: Smaller village setting for the tea ritual, usually with tie-dye demonstrations.

places.name: Yeyu Road Teahouses
places.note: Low-key Old Town teahouses pour the three cups without the full stage show.

food.name: Dali Beer
food.desc: The local Yunnan pilsner brewed at the foot of Cangshan, poured everywhere from lake terraces to Old Town courtyards.

places.name: Renmin Road Bar Strip
places.note: Courtyard bars and rooftops along the lane pour ice-cold Dali beer late.

places.name: Huguo Road Cafes
places.note: Long-running backpacker street; easy spot for a cold beer with Cangshan views.

places.name: Shuanglang Lakefront Bars
places.note: Sunset drinking on the Erhai waterfront, the classic Dali beer setting.

landmarks: Three Pagodas of Chongsheng Temple
Three elegant whitewashed pagodas, the tallest 69 metres and over 1,100 years old, rise against Cangshan's peaks as the enduring symbol of Dali.
Dali Ancient Town
Within restored Ming walls, cobbled streets of Bai courtyard houses, gate towers and lively cafés make the old town Yunnan's most atmospheric base.
Erhai Lake
The ear-shaped alpine lake stretches 40 kilometres beneath the mountains, ringed by a cycling road linking fishing villages, temples and photogenic wetlands.
Cangshan Mountain
Nineteen marble-veined peaks wall the west of Dali, laced by cableways and the cliff-hugging Jade Cloud Path above azalea forests and streams.
Chongsheng Temple
Behind the Three Pagodas, this vast rebuilt royal temple of the Dali Kingdom staircases up the mountainside through halls of gilded Buddhas.
Xizhou Ancient Town
A living museum of Bai architecture famous for its ornate courtyard mansions, morning market and crispy xizhou baba flatbreads.
Shuanglang
Once a fishing village on Erhai's eastern shore, now a laid-back town of boutique inns with the finest sunset views across the lake to Cangshan.
Xiaoputuo Island
A tiny temple-topped islet floating just off Erhai's shore, mobbed by gulls in winter and among the lake's most photographed scenes.
Zhoucheng Village
The heartland of Bai tie-dye, where indigo-stained cloths dry in ancient courtyards and workshops welcome visitors to try the craft.
Butterfly Spring (Hudiequan)
A jade-clear pool beneath an old acacia, celebrated in Bai legend and film for the clouds of butterflies that gather each spring.

train.note: Dali has no international trains. Dali station is in Xiaguan, the modern town about 30-40 minutes by bus from the Old Town, and fast trains from Kunming run roughly hourly and take a little over 2 hours; trains north to Lijiang take about 2 hours and the line west towards Baoshan and eventually Ruili is being extended. Book on 12306 with your passport - Kunming-Dali seats go quickly in summer and over Golden Week, and the through trains from Kunming continue to fill up at Chuxiong.

bus.note: No international coaches serve Dali. Long-distance buses run from the stations in Xiaguan and from a stop by the Old Town's west gate to Kunming (about 4.5 hours), Lijiang and Shangri-La, plus a Monday service to the Shaping market. Tickets are sold at the counters; local buses 4 and 8 link Xiaguan with the Old Town in about an hour, and are the cheapest way between the station and your hotel.

intl.to: Nanzhao Fengqing Island, Xiaoputuo & Shuanglang (China) - Erhai Lake cruise boats from Caicun Wharf near Dali Old Town
intl.op: Erhai Lake cruise services (tickets via Ctrip)

ferry.note: Dali's only boats are the Erhai Lake cruises, which leave from Caicun Wharf a short ride east of the Old Town and from Xiaguan, calling at Nanzhao Fengqing Island and the villages on the far shore. A full circuit takes most of a day and sailings are cut back or cancelled in windy weather and in the winter low season. They are sightseeing cruises rather than scheduled transport, so if you simply want to reach Shuanglang the bus around the lake is quicker.

full.name: Shaxi Ancient Town
full.blurb: Preserved Tea Horse Road trading town with a 2,400-year history, stone bridges, and an original market square.

full.name: Weishan Ancient Town
full.blurb: Little-visited Bai heritage town and cradle of the ancient Nanzhao Kingdom, known for tie-dye textiles and wood carving.
